notes:
ADVERSARIAL READ vs /images/blueprints/factory/4d29fb809a0e__3191__Front_pocket_I_shape_bartack.png.

WHAT THE DRAWING SPECIFIES: a long narrow VERTICAL pocket opening drawn as a slim rectangle, with a magnifier circle at its lower end and an enlarged detail circle beside it. The enlarged detail shows the two vertical edge lines of the opening descending and being joined at the bottom by a dense horizontal RED bar spanning the full width between them — the 'I shape bartack' the filename names. One bar tack, at the closed lower end.

VERIFIED AT 4x ZOOM on the candidate: the bar is a genuine dense satin-stitch bar tack — individual tightly packed stitches with a clean rectangular outline — spanning the full width of the pocket mouth, with the two vertical welt edges rising from each end. The capital-I geometry of the drawing is reproduced exactly. Thread is tonal navy.

ATTEMPTED REJECTIONS THAT FAILED:
(1) Is it a metal rivet or hardware rather than stitching? No — at zoom the individual stitch loops are resolvable; it is thread.
(2) Did it trace the drawing's red? No — the bar is navy, the same colour family as the cloth. No red anywhere in the frame.
(3) Is it a loose zigzag scatter rather than a solid bar? No — the stitches are packed edge to edge into one solid bar with square ends.
(4) Wrong count — a second bar tack at the top end creating a different option? No. The opening's upper end runs into the waistband seam, exactly as the drawing shows it, and carries no second tack.
(5) Wrong pocket geometry borrowed from a sibling option (slant, jeans, curved)? No — the opening is long, narrow and vertical, matching the drawn rectangle.
(6) Wrong garment face? No — trouser front below the waistband, one belt loop visible, correct.
(7) Any annotation traced — magnifier circles, numbers, arrows, callouts? None; the frame is clean cloth only.

No critical or major findings.
